subject: Pricing exhibit — SKU packaging, degression & floor wiring (redlines)
messages:
From: Emma Thompson <emma@bluepeak.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluepeak.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing exhibit — SKU packaging, degression & floor wiring (redlines)

Marcus —

Thanks for the updated order form. Our procurement team reviewed the pricing exhibit and surfaced a few redlines we need Redwood to confirm before we can move to signature. I pasted the key items below and attached our marked-up order form (BluePeak_OrderForm_v2.docx).

Key asks/concerns from BluePeak procurement:
- Degression schedule: we proposed a step-down at month 6. Legal is asking for an explicit performance threshold (monthly usage >= 80% of committed units for prior 60 days) before the step-down applies.
- Floor anchoring: we need clarity that a monthly minimum spend floor cannot be enforced retroactively during the first 90 days after go-live.
- Billing & true-up cadence: prefer quarterly true-ups with a 30-day invoice dispute window (your order form lists monthly true-ups).
- Packaging/sku mapping: the attachment consolidates a few SKUs into a bundle; we want the bundle to inherit the highest-tier degression rate rather than being averaged.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the 90-day no-retroactive-floor carveout and the quarterly true-up? If not, we need a short write-up of Redwood's position so we can present to BluePeak legal.

We are also asking for an explicit fallback if capacity-constrained models are routed (i.e., a temporary preservation of committed rates for 30 days while workloads normalize).

Happy to jump on a quick call if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Emma Thompson
VP, Procurement — BluePeak
emma@bluepeak.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Thompson <emma@bluepeak.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — SKU packaging, degression & floor wiring (redlines)

Emma —

Appreciate the clear summary and the marked-up order form. High level: we can accommodate most of the asks with a small set of guardrails that protect both sides. I attached a quick markup (pricing-exhibit-ML-markup.pdf) that shows the proposed edits inline. TL;DR proposals below to help your legal/procurement review faster:

1) Degression threshold: accept an 80% usage trigger over a rolling 60-day window, with the degression effective at the start of the next billing period after the trigger is satisfied. We will add a clause that prevents gaming (e.g., bulk pre-purchases that are not consumed).

2) Floor anchoring (90-day carveout): we can accept a 90-day non-retroactivity carveout for the floor, provided BluePeak confirms a minimal onboarding forecast and a one-time onboarding credit if actual usage falls 35%+ below forecast in that period. This is to balance the financial exposure on our side for reserved capacity.

3) True-up cadence: we can move to quarterly true-ups with a 30-day dispute window. We recommend maintaining monthly usage reporting (for transparency) but invoices will post quarterly.

4) Bundle SKU treatment: agree to let bundles inherit the highest-tier degression rate, provided bundle composition is fixed for a 90-day assessment window (to avoid frequent repackaging to chase lower rates).

5) Capacity fallback: we will include an operational fallback that preserves committed rates for up to 30 days during short-term routing to a compatible variant; any sustained capacity issues beyond 30 days will trigger a joint remediation plan and optional temporary credit.

If these points look acceptable we can have Legal bake the exact language. If you prefer, I can schedule a 30-minute workshop with your procurement and legal tomorrow or Friday.

Marcus Lin
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0127

Attachment: pricing-exhibit-ML-markup.pdf (pdf, 62 KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 31 May 2028 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — SKU packaging, degression & floor wiring (redlines)

Marcus / Marissa —

Thanks — review notes from Legal below. I pulled the proposed commercial compromises into redline-ready language to reduce back-and-forth. Copying the key snippets we recommend including in the order form (feel free to forward to BluePeak with a note):

1) Degression trigger language (recommended):
"Degression shall only apply after the Customer achieves average usage of at least eighty percent (80%) of the Customer's committed units measured over any rolling sixty (60) day period (the 'Degression Trigger'). If the Degression Trigger is met, the applicable degression rate shall apply beginning on the first day of the next billing cycle."

2) 90-day floor carveout + onboarding credit (recommended):
"Notwithstanding any minimum monthly spend provisions, during the first ninety (90) days following go-live (the 'Onboarding Period') the Provider shall not invoice retroactive floor shortfalls. If actual consumption during the Onboarding Period is thirty-five percent (35%) or more below the Customer's onboarding forecast, the Provider will grant a one-time onboarding credit equal to fifty percent (50%) of the difference between forecasted and actual spend, applied to the first invoice following the Onboarding Period."

3) Quarterly true-up & reporting (recommended):
"Provider shall provide monthly usage reporting. Billing true-ups shall occur on a quarterly basis. Customer shall have thirty (30) days from receipt of a true-up invoice to dispute charges in good faith, during which time undisputed amounts remain payable in accordance with the invoice."

4) Bundled SKU treatment (recommended):
"Where SKUs are sold as a fixed bundle for a period of at least ninety (90) days, the bundle shall inherit the highest degression tier applicable to any component SKU within the bundle. Bundle composition changes shall be subject to mutual written agreement and shall not be used to alter degression applicability retroactively."

5) Short-term capacity fallback (recommended operational clause):
"If Provider temporarily routes requests to a model variant for operational reasons, the Customer's committed pricing shall be preserved for up to thirty (30) days while Provider remedies the operational constraint. If the constraint extends beyond thirty (30) days, Parties shall convene promptly to agree on remediation steps and any applicable credits."

Risk note: the onboarding credit mitigates customer churn risk but exposes Redwood to initial utilization shortfall. The 35% threshold and 50% credit balances protection for both sides; confirm whether Sales is comfortable with that multiplier.

If Sales signs off, Legal will prepare a tracked-change order form and send over a .txt redline in the next business day.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Second, the 35% threshold is acceptable but can we limit the onboarding credit to a one-time application per customer (i.e., not per bundle)?

We are happy to take your tracked redline and route to BluePeak legal. Can we do a 30-minute call on Monday (June 5) at 11:00 AM PT to walk through the final language and, if agreed, confirm a DocuSign timeline?
